title: Tiered fallback runbook and rollout decision queue
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact runbook for small-to-medium releases where we apply a tiered fallback strategy (model variant -> region fallback -> degrade service -> rollback). It combines a short week-by-week rollout calendar with the operational decision queue, preflight checklist, and a minimal rollback matrix. Target audience: release conductor, on-call SRE, model-owner, product PM.

Quick context (notes to self):
- Goal: ship variant B (quantized, 8-bit) for low-latency tier while keeping A (fp16) as automatic fallback.
- Release size: ~5% traffic initial, can scale to 25% over 72h if all gates green.
- Avoid big-bang in APAC region until US and EU pass 48h stability gates.

Release micro-calendar (compact):
- Day -7 (prep): finalize canary prompts, register perf-run artifacts, notify CS and partners. Owner: Maya
- Day -3: deploy variant B to canary pool (subset of internal traffic). Run synthetic traffic harness for 4h. Owner: Ravi
- Day 0 (launch window): 05:00-07:00 UTC baseline checks; 08:00 set traffic to 5% globally except APAC; begin 02:00 UTC overlay alarms. Owner: Diego
- Day 1: evaluate telemetry, run qualitative prompt set (top 50 prompts). Decide whether to increase to 10% at 12:00 UTC. Decision due by 11:00 UTC.
- Day 2: if gates clear, 10% -> 15% at 14:00 UTC. APAC routing still disabled.
- Day 3-5: steady 15% with automated sampling every 2h; by Day 5 consider APAC soft-open at 2% for 24h.
- Day 7: final decision to escalate to production rollout or roll forward with fixes.

Preflight checklist (must be green before Day 0):
- [ ] Smoke test: synthetic token-per-sec profile within 10% of baseline
- [ ] Latency P95 <= SLO for 95% of hosts
- [ ] Cost estimator plugin run (expected cost delta documented in release notes)
- [ ] Model variant pinned in registry and checksum verified
- [ ] Canary key rotation script validated (rotation window configured)
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards live and bookmarked: latency, errors, token cost, tail latencies, KV cache hit-rate
- [ ] Ops channel (#deployments) notified with runbook link + anchor times
- [ ] Customer success notified (CS-runbook excerpt attached)
- [ ] Rollback play and runbook pre-warmed (see rollback matrix)

Gating criteria (simple pass/fail per day):
- Safety: no customer-facing regressions flagged by CS and internal QA (binary)
- Latency: rolling 6h P95 not exceeding baseline by >15%
- Errors: total 6h 5xx rate < 0.1% above baseline or < 50 absolute events
- Quality: prompt-set automated eval delta < 2% BLEU-style / task-specific metric (owner defined)
- Cost: per-token unit cost change within acceptable band defined by finance

Tiered fallback semantics (what happens automatically):
1) Model variant fallback: if host error spike > threshold, runtime will route requests to fp16 variant automatically (A).
2) Regional fallback: when a whole AZ/region experiences latency > 2x SLO for 15m, traffic is rerouted to healthy regions (subject to routing policy and legal constraints).
3) Degraded mode: enable log-sampling and reduced prompt truncation to lower load (manual opt-in).
4) Full rollback: if multiple gates fail consecutively (see rollback matrix), revert to previous model and capacity configuration.

Rollback matrix (simplified):
- Trigger: sustained P95 > 2x SLO for 30m -> Action: immediate 100% revert to variant A for affected shard. Owner: on-call SRE.
- Trigger: quality regression > 5% on core prompt set or critical customer complaint escalated -> Action: pause rollout, patch and re-canary. Owner: model-owner & PM.
- Trigger: cost spike leading to >30% daily unit cost increase -> Action: throttle non-critical routes, hold rollout. Owner: infra-cost team.

Decision queue (how decisions get made during Day 0-7):
- Inputs queued to the decision board: telemetry snippets (link), sample prompts (link), CS escalations (JIRA id).
- Triage rhythm: 09:00, 13:00, 17:00 UTC checks (owners: SRE, Model Owner, PM). Each triage must record a binary Accept/Hold/Abort and rationale.
- Fast-abort rule: if two independent owners vote Abort within 60m, trigger rollback.

Telemetry thresholds & quick queries (examples):
- Query: P95 by pool last 30m -> alert if > threshold.
- Query: cache hit-rate drop > 10% -> possible cold-start issue.
- Query: output token distribution shift (new logits) -> flag for model quality review.

Communication templates (short):
- Ops channel update (example): "Deploy Day 0: 08:00 UTC -> 5% global (no APAC). Current status: green. Key metrics: P95 210ms (+4%), errors 0.02%. Decision at 11:00 UTC to scale to 10%."
- External release note blurb (draft): "We’re rolling out a latency-optimized model variant to a small share of traffic. Expect small improvements in response times for the low-latency tier; no change to data residency or privacy. We’ll update if we extend coverage."

Open items / TODOs (explicit, prioritized):
1) Validate APAC legal routing constraints for model fallback (Priya).
2) Add canary prompt set that includes long-context prompts (Ravi).
3) Hook cost-estimator alert to #finance-alerts (Diego).
4) Build a small UI tile in console for rollout decisions (nice-to-have, backlog).

Postmortem anchors (if we roll back or see issues):
- Time window to capture: full 48h pre and post rollout windows.
- Minimum evidence: raw request samples (anonymized), telemetry snapshots, CS tickets, on-call notes.
- Postmortem owner: release conductor (Maya) with SRE and model-owner co-authors.

Notes on minimal experiments:
- If we are uncertain about perf/cost, run an A/B split on non-critical routes only for 24h (max 2% traffic). This reduces blast radius while yielding signal.

Bottom line checklist (one-liner before flip to 5%):
- Preflight green, telemetry dashboards up, CS notified, rollback plan staged, decision crew present.

—— end of draft runbook ———

Remember: keep this short and iterative; this doc is the quick operating canvas that should be referenced from the canonical Confluence page above. If anything in this runbook is disputed during a rollout, default to safety-first (pause and escalate).
